title: Suppress ghost host table entries after VPC peering switchover causing intermittent cross-tenant DNS answers
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customer 'AcadiaHealth' reported intermittent DNS responses that resolved to IPs belonging to a different tenant immediately after scheduled VPC peering reconfigures. Impact is production traffic misrouting for DNS (both UDP and TCP) for a subset of requests during peering switchover windows. This ticket tracks investigation, short-term mitigations, and the long-term dataplane/control-plane fix to prevent stale host mappings from being used after peering changes.
impact: High: production customers intermittently received DNS answers pointing at other tenant endpoints leading to failed connections and blocked application flows. Reported by 2 enterprise tenants; risk of data leakage perceived by customers.
reproduction_steps: 1) Setup two tenants A and B in Dedicated with active VPC peering between their overlay networks.
2) From tenant A, resolve customer-hostname that maps to an IP in A; confirm normal resolution.
3) Trigger peering reconfiguration (simulate controlled failover/peering-swapping event).
4) Within the next 30s-3min window, some DNS responses observed to include A-records that route to B's overlay host entries.
5) Observed on both UDP and TCP DNS; probability increases with concurrent short-lived flows and high churn of ephemeral SNAT ports.
mitigation_actions: 1) Hotfix deployed to control-plane: on peering change, emit explicit host-unlearn messages to dataplane (rolled out to 5% of Dedicated clusters).
2) Temporary aggressive host TTL scavenger: reduce stale overlay host entry TTL to 5s for peering-change window (config flag).
3) Applied customer-level policy: temporarily force DNS queries through region fallback route for affected tenants until stabilized.
4) SE communicated mitigation and timeline to AcadiaHealth; established monitoring dashboard and 1:1 escalation channel.
root_cause: When VPC peering interfaces are torn down and reattached rapidly, dataplane host learning can retain stale overlay host->tunnel mappings. During the transient reconciliation window the forwarding logic did not validate peering affinity, causing responses to be sent using stale L2/L3 mappings. This was exacerbated by a race in the control-plane where host-unlearn events were buffered and lost under bursty peering reconcilations.
proposed_fix: 1) Ensure control-plane always emits reliable host-unlearn notifications on peering teardown and that they are acked by dataplane; add sequence numbers to peering events. 2) Add conservative dataplane validation: if a host mapping age > X or peering-state changed for that tenant, prefer route-revalidation before using mapping. 3) Add integration test that simulates rapid peering swaps and asserts zero cross-tenant forwarding. 4) Add observability: per-host learned_at timestamp and peering-affinity tag surfaced to Console.
proposed_fix_tradeoffs: Acked host-unlearn increases control-plane RPCs under mass peering churn; sequence numbers add protocol complexity but prevent silent loss. Dataplane validation adds a small latency penalty on cold lookups; we will gate aggressive validation behind a tenant-scoped rollout and instrumentation to measure impact.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (immediate): continue aggressive TTL scavenger and keep emergency control-plane hotfix enabled for affected clusters.
Phase 1 (canary): deploy control-plane host-unlearn reliability and sequence numbers to 10% of Dedicated clusters with synthetic peering churn test harness enabled.
Phase 2 (ramp): enable dataplane validation checks behind feature flag, ramp 25% -> 50% -> 100% with metrics on DNS latency and resolution correctness.
Phase 3 (GA): remove temporary scavenger, expose monitoring to Console, update runbook and customer-facing incident note.
Rollback: revert feature flag and host-unlearn change; re-enable scavenger if regression detected.
qa_criteria: Automated integration test that simulates peering up/down 100x and asserts zero cross-tenant DNS answers.
No increase >5% in 95th percentile DNS resolution latency after dataplane validation enabled.
Can reproduce mitigation effect being able to eliminate cross-tenant mapping within expected TTL window in staging.
Executive summary and runbook reviewed by SRE and Networking owners.
